assumptions.font: monospace resolves to JetBrainsMono Nerd Font via default/fontconfig/conf.avail/50-omarchy.conf:332-335, package ttf-jetbrains-mono-nerd-basic (install/omarchy-base.packages:149). Nerd Font codepoints below assume that font.

assumptions.dispatcher output: Tables for `omarchy <group>` were rendered by replaying the dispatcher's own metadata parsing (bin/omarchy:173-317) and table printer (bin/omarchy:633-652, 868-891) over bin/ headers at this commit. The dispatcher itself was not executed. Row order follows `sort -u`; for the groups shown, C and en_US collation give the same order.
assumptions.not in repo: The Neovim/LazyVim configuration ships in the separate omarchy-nvim package (docs/file-layout.md:25-27; install/omarchy-base.packages:102). Lazygit's config is an empty file (config/lazygit/config.yml, 0 bytes). Cliamp has no config here. Their screens are upstream defaults and are not specified here.

terminal.layout: One foot window per terminal, tiled by default. SUPER+RETURN runs omarchy-launch-terminal with the focused window's pid, so the new terminal opens in that terminal's working directory (default/hypr/bindings/applications.lua:2; default/hypr/helpers.lua:173-185; bin/omarchy-launch-terminal:12). Foot draws a 14x14 px pad of background colour around the cell grid. Text is JetBrainsMono Nerd Font at size 9 (foot sizes are points). The cursor is a steady block: the cell under it is drawn in the background colour on a bright_foreground block. 10000 lines of scrollback. The palette comes from the theme's generated foot.ini, which foot.ini includes. The window is opaque unless the Glassy option rewrites alpha to 0.65. A theme switch recolours running foot windows live by writing OSC colour sequences to each shell's pty; nothing is restarted.

shell.layout: A fresh terminal prints nothing before the prompt: no motd, no fastfetch, no banner. The rc chain (default/bash/rc) only sets env, history, aliases, functions and integrations; none of it echoes. The first-run welcome is a desktop notification, not terminal output. The prompt is Starship (see the prompt section). History is appended on exit (histappend), 32768 entries. Up and Down search history by the typed prefix. Tab cycles through candidates (menu-complete) after first completing the common prefix, case-insensitively. `ls` is eza in long form with a header row (eza's -h is --header), icons and directories first. `cd` goes through zoxide: a path that exists is a plain cd, anything else is a zoxide jump that then prints a folder glyph and the new pwd.

prompt.layout: Starship, one line, no user, host or clock. In the home directory the prompt reads `~ ❯ ` with both the tilde and the chevron in bold cyan (manual/14-omarchy-cli.md:10 shows `~ ❯ omarchy`). Outside a repo, the path is cut to its last 2 components, prefixed `…/` when truncated, in starship's default directory style, then a space. Inside a git repo, the repo root name is bold cyan, followed by the path within it, a space, the branch in italic cyan with a trailing space, any status symbols in cyan, and the chevron. After a failed command the chevron becomes ✗, still bold cyan. add_newline=true puts a blank line between prompts. Command timeout is 200 ms.

omarchy_cli.layout: `omarchy` is a dispatcher over the 574 omarchy-* scripts in bin/. Each script's header comments (`# omarchy:summary=`, `args=`, `group=`, `name=`, `alias=`, `hidden=`) give its route and help. `omarchy` or `omarchy --help` prints the main help. `omarchy <group>` prints a group table: a header `<Group> commands — <description>:`, then rows of `  <usage padded to the widest>  <summary>`. `omarchy <route> --help` prints Usage/summary/Arguments/Examples/Aliases/Binary. Words map to binaries (`omarchy theme set X` runs omarchy-theme-set X). A command that requires arguments and gets none prints its help instead of running. An unknown route prints three lines on stderr and exits 127. Most mutating commands print nothing on success: their effect is visual (theme, background, bar) or a desktop notification. Commands that print are listed with their exact strings.

fastfetch.layout: About (Omarchy menu > About, or `omarchy launch about`) is a floating, centred foot window with app-id org.omarchy.about. On first launch it is 920x480. After that it is resized to hug the content and the fitted size is remembered. The cursor is hidden and the screen cleared, then fastfetch runs with /etc/fastfetch/config.jsonc, and any keypress closes the window. The logo is the file ~/.config/omarchy/branding/about.txt, seeded from icon.txt: a 54-column by 26-row block-glyph Omarchy mark in ANSI green. Fastfetch pads the logo 2 rows from the top, 2 columns from the left and 6 columns before the module column. The module column starts with two blank rows, then three boxed sections, each a dim (\e[90m) 54-column frame. The Hardware section has green keys, the Software section blue keys, and the Age/Uptime/Update section magenta keys. Each section's first key is an icon plus a label (' PC', ' OS', '󱦟 OS Age'). Later keys are tree glyphs '│ ├' plus an icon, and the last key in a section uses '└ └'. Values follow the key after fastfetch's default separator. A blank row separates sections, and one blank row ends the layout. A periodic 'sheen' animation glints across the logo. Key glyphs are Nerd Font codepoints listed per item.

btop.layout: Activity is btop. SUPER+SHIFT+T opens it with `omarchy-launch-tui btop`, so the window has app-id org.omarchy.btop and floats centred at 875x600. Four boxes are shown: cpu, mem, net and proc. With btop's default arrangement, cpu runs across the top, mem and net stack on the left below it, and proc fills the right; that arrangement is upstream, not set here. Corners are rounded. Graphs use braille symbols and refresh every 2000 ms. Processes are sorted by 'cpu lazy' and coloured with a gradient, with per-process mini CPU graphs. Battery, CPU watts, temperatures, frequency and uptime are shown. vim keys are on. Colours come from the theme's btop.theme via ~/.config/btop/themes/current.theme, and theme_background=true paints the main background.

neovim.layout: Typing `n` (or `nvim`) runs Neovim with the omarchy-nvim LazyVim setup. That package is outside this repo, so its start screen (dashboard header, menu entries and keys) and statusline are not specified here. LazyVim's upstream defaults apply, plus whatever omarchy-nvim changes. This repo supplies only the colorscheme: each theme's neovim.lua is a lazy.nvim spec that sets LazyVim's colorscheme. Themes without one get the template, which uses omacom/aether.nvim (branch v3) fed the theme palette. The leader key is Space, as the manual describes. SUPER+SHIFT+N opens the default editor in a new terminal.

tuis.layout: Omarchy 4 ships few TUIs. Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and audio moved into shell panels: there is no impala, bluetui or wiremix anywhere in the repo, and the manual says so. Bound TUIs: btop (SUPER+SHIFT+T, floating), cliamp (SUPER+SHIFT+ALT+M, launch-or-focus, tiled), lazydocker (SUPER+SHIFT+D, only if installed; not in the base packages), tmux in the Work session (SUPER+ALT+RETURN) and herdr (SUPER+CTRL+RETURN). Lazygit is installed but has no key binding; you run `lazygit` or press Space g g in Neovim. Its config file is empty, so it shows upstream defaults. Every TUI runs inside foot, so it uses the terminal palette above.

home.layout: A fresh user's home holds Documents, Downloads, Music, Pictures, Videos and Work (Work/tries inside it). Desktop, Templates and Public are pointed at $HOME and removed. Projects is only a GTK bookmark and is not created. The dotfiles (.bashrc, .config/..., .local/...) come from /etc/skel and are hidden from plain `ls`. Because `ls` is eza -lh, `ls ~` prints a header row (Permissions Size User Date Modified Name, from eza's -h = --header) and then a long listing of the six directories, each with a folder icon, directories first. The exact columns are eza's upstream defaults.

notes: Runtime: `omarchy version` prints pacman's version for the omarchy package. The repo's version file reads 4.0.0.alpha (version:1), but the packaged string (pkgrel etc.) cannot be read from the repo. A demo could show '4.0.0.alpha'.

Runtime: fastfetch module values (host model, CPU name and cores, GPU, display resolution, disk 'used / total (percent) - fs', memory, swap, kernel, WM 'Hyprland (Wayland)', DE, terminal 'foot', packages count, wmtheme, terminal font 'JetBrainsMono Nerd Font (9pt)') use fastfetch's own upstream formats. The config sets only keys, colours and the GPU format. The separator between key and value is fastfetch's default; the config does not set display.separator.

Runtime: the theme swatch row emits \e[38m before the first dot. That is an incomplete extended-colour SGR, so how the first dot is coloured depends on foot's parser. The other seven dots are white, cyan, magenta, blue, yellow, green and red (SGR 37..31) (etc/fastfetch/config.jsonc:122).

Runtime: the 'Dev branch' row (omarchy-version-branch) exits 1 on a packaged install (bin/omarchy-version-branch:9), so fastfetch's command module prints nothing for it. Whether the key still shows is fastfetch's behaviour, not specified here.
Runtime: About's sheen animation (bin/omarchy-branding-about-animation) repaints logo cells in frames. Its timing constants live in that file and were not extracted here.

Upstream: Starship's default directory style (applied outside a repo root), add_newline behaviour on the very first prompt, and the exact eza column layout are upstream defaults, not set in this repo.

Upstream: LazyVim's dashboard (header art, entries such as Find File / New File / Recent Files / Config / Restore Session / Lazy Extras / Lazy / Quit and their keys) is a LazyVim/snacks.nvim default. omarchy-nvim may override it. Neither ships in this repo, so the spec makes no claim about it.

Interactive: `omarchy theme switcher`, `omarchy background`, `omarchy menu`, `omarchy pkg install` and `omarchy debug` open overlays or gum/fzf pickers rather than printing text. A demo should map them to the desktop overlay or a canned picker.
Dispatcher subtlety: `omarchy menu --help` gets the dispatcher's generic command help (bin/omarchy:1039-1055). Only `omarchy menu help` reaches the script's own usage block (bin/omarchy-menu:32-46).

Dispatcher subtlety: `omarchy theme set` with no name prints the dispatcher's command help, because args are required (bin/omarchy:1058-1070). The script's own 'Usage: omarchy-theme-set <theme-name>' appears only when run directly as omarchy-theme-set.

omarchy update writes its whole session to /tmp/omarchy-update.log via script(1) (bin/omarchy-update:56-59). Inside the gum box, bullets are '• ' and the border is gum's 'normal' style (bin/omarchy-update-confirm:5-11).
Name clash: 'Starship' is both the prompt (config/starship.toml) and a theme (themes/starship). The theme uses the aether template for Neovim.

Upstream: in eza, -h means --header, so every `ls` begins with a column header row. -l without --no-user shows permissions, size, user, date and name. Column set and date format are eza defaults (default/bash/aliases:3).
